title: zoe-bench result
description: One run of zoe-bench load or zoe-bench saturate against a ZEO server. Results are numbers about a synthetic corpus, never data. The document holds no host name, user name or path.

steps.description: The steps, with more clients at each step: 1, 2, 4 and on, then max_clients. The last step is the first one over the ceiling, or the step of max_clients.

loads_per_second_under_ceiling.description: loads_per_second of the last step whose load_p99_seconds is at most the ceiling, or null when no step is under it.

clients_under_ceiling.description: The clients of the same step, or null.

schema_version.description: The version of this schema. A change that a reader of the previous version cannot read increments it.

machine.description: The machine that runs the clients. The server can run on another machine. It holds no host name, user name or path.

name.description: A slug of ZOE_BENCH_MACHINE, or a slug of the CPU model.

logical_cpus.description: The CPUs that the process can use.

memory_bytes.description: The physical memory, or 0 when the system does not show it.

started.description: When the run started, in UTC.

commit.description: ZOE_BENCH_COMMIT when it is a commit id, else null.

storage.description: The storage name that each client gives to register.

pipeline.description: The most loadBefore calls in flight for one client.

objects.description: The number of objects that the run creates first.

txn_size.description: The number of different objects that each transaction reads.

write_ratio.description: The probability that a transaction writes back its objects.

zipf.description: The exponent of the Zipf law that picks the objects. 0 is uniform; 1.0 is the hot-spot case.

seed.description: The seed of the schedules of the clients. The same seed gives the same schedules.

object_size.description: The size of the pickle of each object, in bytes.

clients.description: The number of clients, each with its own connection.

transactions.description: The number of transactions of each client.

max_clients.description: The most clients of a step.

p99_ceiling_seconds.description: The ceiling of the p99 of loadBefore, in seconds. The default is the number of N3, but a run on a small store is not an N3 verdict: N3 is a cache miss on a 10 GB store.

warmup_seconds.description: The time at the start of each step that does not count.

step_seconds.description: The time of each step after the warm-up.

transactions.description: The most transactions of each client in a step after the warm-up, or null for no limit. A step ends at the end of its time or at this limit.

measure.description: The numbers of one run of the workload by a number of clients. A retry runs a transaction again after a conflict at its vote, and each retry counts.

transactions.description: The transactions of all clients that count: each one commits or only reads. The warm-up of a saturate step does not count.

commits.description: The transactions that wrote and committed.

conflicts.description: The votes that failed with a conflict.

retries.description: The attempts after the first one of each transaction.

conflicts_per_1000_commits.description: conflicts times 1,000, divided by commits; null without a commit.

elapsed_seconds.description: The time from the start of the clients, or from the end of the warm-up of a saturate step, to the end of the last client.

load_p50_seconds.description: The median time of a loadBefore call, from the send of the call to its reply.

load_p99_seconds.description: The 99th percentile of the same times, by the nearest rank.

load_max_seconds.description: The longest of the same times.

lock_wait_p50_seconds.description: The median time of a vote, where the server takes the locks of the oids and waits for them; null without a vote.

lock_wait_p99_seconds.description: The 99th percentile of the same times; null without a vote.

step.description: One step of a saturate run: its clients and its numbers.
